DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Fifteen Kilos on a Bed

STS-HS11-L4-13001400-HSSCIENG1112-STP-IMR-01 • HS Science Engineering Design 11-12 • Qualitative and Quantitative Criteria and Constraints
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In a pitch competition a team gets a few minutes to convince judges to fund one design and nothing else. Farida, Omid, and Zarina took every number on that board from their own first week in this city, when each of them arrived with one bag and did homework on a flattened cardboard box. Fifty five centimeters is the size the airline let them carry. Fifteen kilos is what a stack of borrowed schoolbooks weighs.
The judges add one more requirement. The desk has to feel steady when you lean on it. Is that something you can measure with a number, or something you can only describe in words? Say which, and say why.
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Farida doing?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about Farida in precise language, cite the exact detail that proves it, and explain what that detail signals about the team's priorities.
2
What is Omid holding?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about the object Omid holds in precise language, cite the exact detail that proves it, and explain what problem it stands for.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about the teacher in precise language, cite the exact detail that proves it, and explain which line on the wall his work is aimed at.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about this place in precise language, cite two exact details that prove it, and explain why one is stronger evidence than the other.
5
Tell me about the board.
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about the board in precise language, cite its exact wording, and explain the difference between what its two sides ask for.
6
What is Zarina wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify your answer about Zarina's clothing in precise language, cite the exact detail that proves it, and explain what it tells you about conditions in this space.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: NGSS HS-ETS1-1 — Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
